3e5710y9.name: Northern heartland
3e5710y9.story: The human start. New-woken Wakers come to at Wakewell Abbey and find a farming country six years after the Council's revolution: the old Tennely land, its promises half kept, its tithes high and everybody counting. The trouble is people, the Council and the old guard, with kobolds and wildlife as the honest monsters.
themes: Waking: the Abbey, where the Dream touches the world, helps the new-woken onto their feet. Gentle, odd and a little sad.

The revolution's heartland: the Council took the colony six years ago and promised to break up the Tennely estates, sell the land cheap and set fair tithes. The tithes are higher, the land went to the Council's friends, and the Tennelys' summer house is a Council granary under guard.
The cliff and the forest above: loggers work the cliff foot, kobolds dig into it, and elves watch from the top and don't come down.
The north road: Nordish herders and traders drift south along it, friendly and competing.
3e5710y9.ground: West, farm lowland down to the coast, rolling in low swells, never quite flat. East, the plateau's cliff, about 400 ft high with the High forest on top, rising over a band of steep, broken foothills. The Prow, a lower step of the plateau about 200 ft high, juts west from the cliff into the middle of the zone as a steep, rugged ridge, with ponds under its west end and a small falls dropping off it into the biggest. The cascade comes off the plateau south of the Prow and falls in two drops: onto a ledge with a small pool partway down the cliff, then from the ledge's lip into a lake at the cliff foot. The Lake river runs west from the lake, gathers the middle valley's streams below Hallam's cross, and runs past Brightford to the sea. North, crags along the border, with Tennely Hall's valley running up into them to the north pass, and the north stream running from the valley west along their foot to the sea. North-east, a basin under the cliff, drained west by the cliff brook to the Prow's ponds. A low wooded rise runs north to south west of Hallam's cross. Crags run along the south border too, crossed where the south road, the stepping stones and the lake road go out. The Abbey on a bench above the lake's north-east shore, in the pocket between the Prow, the plateau cliff and the lake: one way out, west along the north shore.
neighbours: South: Southern heartland (10-20), over the crags from Brightford's ford, and south-east round the lake's south shore. From the cliff foot there, a trail climbs the face to the falls ledge, where the Underfall's cave is.
North: Northwest coast (18-28), up the north road from Northgate past Tennely Hall and over the north pass.
East, up the cliff: High forest (22-32), and the Cascade wood (12-20) above the falls. Seen, never reached from here.
3e5710y9.progression: Abbey (1-4), Hallam's cross (4-6), Brightford (5-9), Wrackholm (6-8) up the coast from Brightford, then north-east to Cliffside camp (6-9) or north to Tennely Hall and Northgate (8-10). You leave south over the crags from Brightford, south-east round the lake, or north over the pass.
3e5710y9.mainThread: The tithe and the Greycoats: the revolution's promises against the old guard, with no clean side. Heroes fight Slade's band, never the Greycoats or the Council.
parts: The Abbey and the lake: the pocket under the Prow and the plateau cliff, with the lakeshore and the falls pool under the cascade's lower drop, quiet and odd. Closed by cliffs north and east and the lake south. Opens west along the north shore, between the Prow and the lake, to Hallam's cross.
Hallam's farms: open barley and hedges round the crossroads, between the middle valley's streams, in the middle of the zone, with the Prow's ponds to the east. Opens to every other part.

Brightford and the river: the town at the ford on the river's south bank, the river meadows, the rolling south-west lowland and the south crags behind. Opens east up the river to Hallam's cross, north over the ford up the coast plain, and out south over the crags.
The cliff foot: the loggers' basin north of the Prow, under the plateau cliff, with the kobold diggings in the cliff. Opens south-west down the cliff brook to the ponds and Hallam's cross.

The north valley: Tennely Hall's valley running up into the northern crags, with Slade's camp and the burned lodge, watched. Opens south down the valley to Hallam's cross, west along the north stream to Northgate, and north over the pass.

The north road: the coast plain from Brightford's ford up to Northgate under the north-west crags, with Wrackholm in its cove under Gull Head on the coast, where Northgate beck comes down to the north stream. Opens east along the crag foot to Tennely Hall's valley.
barriers: The Prow, hard: a lower step of the plateau, a steep, rugged ridge jutting west from the cliff between the Abbey and Cliffside camp, with ponds under its west end. You go round its west end.
The Lake river, soft: from the lake west to the sea, crossed at Brightford's ford, by the lake road below the lake, and by the stepping stones below Hallam's cross.
The northern crags, hard: crags along the north border, crossed only by the north pass at the head of Tennely Hall's valley.
The rise, soft: a low wooded ridge west of Hallam's cross, between the farms and the coast plain, gone round at either end.
The lake, hard: the lake and the cliff close the Abbey's pocket to the south and east. The only way in is along the north shore.
The south crags, hard: steep crags along the south border, crossed only by the south road, the stepping stones and the lake road round the lake's south shore.
The plateau cliff, hard: about 400 ft of cliff over steep foothills along the whole east side, never climbed from here, except the trail to the falls ledge.

yrm6ylej.name: Wakewell Abbey
yrm6ylej.what: The spawn. Keepers, a dormitory where Wakers come to, a small chapel, a herb garden, a hen yard and two rowboats on the lake.
yrm6ylej.where: On a bench above the lake's north-east shore, under the plateau cliff, looking across the water to the falls.
yrm6ylej.mood: Gentle, odd and a little sad. Short of hands: the Council's levy took the lay brothers for the gap, so the Wakers do the chores.
people: Assessor Pell Duvane, the Council's assessor counting the stores
lines: The new-woken (1-4): fight, gather and talk; ends with the first dream and a send-off to Hallam's cross
The glowdiggers (4-8) starts here: kobold sneaks steal candles and drop glowing glass
nearby: The falls pool: dream-wisps and dreamroot (the Dream's locus)
The lakeshore: lamp rushes, foxes at the hen yard
Kobold sneaks' burrows in the cliff's north end
yrm6ylej.site: Dry ground on a bench some 45 ft over the lake, sloping gently to the shore, with the lake for water.
yrm6ylej.situation: The falls: where the cascade comes off the plateau into the lake, the Dream's touch on the world.
yrm6ylej.scene: The Abbey stands on a bench about 60 ft over the lake, its front door facing south down the road from Hallam's cross. The forecourt has the well house, and Brannick waits on the road. The herb garden lies south-west of the door, with its cabbage and pumpkin rows, drying herbs and a bench, where Nell works. The hen yard is west of the wing, fenced, with the hen house and two coops, facing the fox country on the west shore. The woodshed stands north-west of the wing. The graveyard lies behind the nave, with its crypt and lychgate. Its spirit healer stands between the two. A trail runs down from the forecourt to the dock, which has two rowboats, where Aubin sets Wakers to sleep by the water. Inside, the Abbess greets the new-woken at the nave door. Wenna keeps the refectory, and the cells above are the rest area. Pell counts stores in the refectory.

aesl88uw.name: Hallam's cross
aesl88uw.what: Three farm families round a shrine at a crossroads, behind on their tithe. The militia took the shrine's bell as scrap for the gap.
aesl88uw.where: Crossroads farms between the middle valley's streams, in the middle of the zone, where the ways from the Abbey, Brightford, the cliff foot and the hills meet.
aesl88uw.mood: Proud and worn. They're right that the Council's measure is false.
people: Wenna Hallam, head of the Hallams
Grandsire Tobin Hallam, the old man who remembers the old lord's day
lines: The tithe (4-9) starts here: short sacks against a false measure
The Greycoats (6-10) is seeded here: grain left on the step by someone in a grey coat
nearby: Barns with rats, barley with boars
Hedge apples for cider, the one thing the Council doesn't count
aesl88uw.site: Low farmland between the streams that come down from the north valley and the Prow's ponds, with a brook at the door.
aesl88uw.situation: A crossroads: the zone's ways all meet here, above where the streams gather and run down to the river.
aesl88uw.scene: Five ways meet at the shrine, a wayside shrine with a bench and bluebells, its bell gone to the militia. The Hallams farm the north-east wedge: their farmhouse faces the cross, with the hen house, a big barn, a haystack and the hedge-apple trees where Tobin keeps his cider barrels. The windmill stands in the north wedge. The Cobbs hold the north-west, toward the stream: a farmhouse, Dunstan's smithy, where he mends carts and gear, and a woodshed where Orla hangs her game. The Rusks hold the south-west: the farmhouse they let to travellers, the inn, with a pig shed, a granary and barley rows with a scarecrow. The crossroads graveyard lies in the south-east wedge, off the road.

e5uogbb6.name: Brightford
e5uogbb6.what: The zone's town, called Tennelford until the revolution. Inn, vendors, trainers, the reeve's hall, a tithe barn, a militia post with a lock-up, and the Tennelys' statue lying toppled in the square.
e5uogbb6.where: On the south bank of the Lake river at its lowest ford, the way south through the crags to the Southern heartland.
e5uogbb6.mood: Busy and careful. The Council's seat here, and the old guard's memories in the same square.
people: Reeve Odile Marchbank, the Council's reeve
Old Bertil, the old guard veteran
Jory Venn, a Greycoat in the lock-up
Hettie Croft, who wants the statue's plaque kept
a scrap dealer, who wants it sold
lines: The tithe (4-9): the reeve's standard, Varn's scales and ledger; Varn is moved, not punished
The Greycoats (6-10): robbers in grey coats on the north road, and Jory Venn's message
nearby: Farms south of the road, for weighing tithe sacks
e5uogbb6.forces: The Council's locus: requisitions out to every farm and the Abbey, grain wagons out to Tennely Hall.
breadcrumbs: To Cliffside camp: the loggers need hands
To Tennely Hall: the granary needs a guard
Out south over the ford to the Southern heartland
e5uogbb6.site: Low meadow on the south bank, a few feet over the river, with the south crags behind it.
e5uogbb6.situation: The lowest ford on the Lake river, where the south road over the crags meets the river road to the coast and the way north to the farms.
e5uogbb6.scene: The road comes over the ford from the north-east and turns south past the town. Brightford sits east of the bend round a grass market square, where the Tennelys' statue lies toppled among the stalls: Jessa Thorne's leather and bows, Ludo Crake's scrap, and a well. The reeve's hall closes the square on the east, with the jettied tailor's shop to its north-west, toward the river. Moll Abernathy's inn faces the square from the south, the stone shop stands at its west corner by the road, and town houses, the apothecary's among them, line the lane behind the inn. West of the road the militia post holds the lock-up, with stocks, a banner and a wanted poster out front, and the smithy beside it. The tithe barn stands east of the inn, and the graveyard lies beyond it on the rise, off the road.

r322s8fi.name: Cliffside camp
r322s8fi.what: A logging camp with a log chute down from a ledge.
r322s8fi.where: On the north-east basin's floor by the cliff brook, under the plateau cliff, between the farmland and the forest above.
r322s8fi.mood: Loud and honest, sick of the Council's quotas and of arrows from above.
people: Foreman Gus Tarrant, the logging foreman
Ithriel, the elven warden, who comes down to the ledge once
lines: The glowdiggers (4-8): kobolds dug into an Age of Light chamber in the cliff and worship its glowing glass; the Glowmother hoards it
The cliff wardens (7-10): arrows at the chute; the cutting undermines the trees that hold the cliff; ends with a no-cut line
nearby: The kobold diggings, outside and in, with the elven chamber deepest
r322s8fi.forces: Kobolds' locus in the cliff foot nearby; the elven wardens' on the cliff top above.
breadcrumbs: South round the lake to the Southern heartland, and the trail up the cliff face to the falls ledge
r322s8fi.site: Flat basin floor by the brook that runs west from the cliff foot, with the cliff for the log chute.
r322s8fi.situation: The edge between the farmland and the forest above: the only place the loggers can bring timber down.
r322s8fi.scene: The road from the farmland ends at a fire ring on the flat by the cliff brook, with benches round it, where Nan Brewis feeds the camp and Wakers sleep by the fire. Foreman Tarrant's cabin stands to the north-west and the cookhouse to the north-east, with the loggers' big tents between them and west of the fire. North of the camp the log chute runs down the slope from the ledge to the log piles at its foot. The lumber mill stands east by the brook, with Ossie Wrenfield's timber crane, plank stacks, a saw bench and sawdust, and the woodshed sits south-west by the road. Stumps dot the cleared ground all round. The camp's few dead lie in a small fenced plot to the north-west, off the road.

d908slex.name: Tennely Hall
d908slex.what: The Tennelys' old summer house, now a Council granary with a garrison.
d908slex.where: Up the north valley under the northern crags, out of sight of the farms, at the end of the grain road and the foot of the north pass.
d908slex.mood: Rigid and uneasy. Its captain served the Tennelys and serves the Council now.
people: Captain Wystan Hale, the granary's captain
lines: The Greycoats (6-10) ends here: Slade's tally, his camp and Slade himself; the Greycoats' captain thanks you at the burned lodge
nearby: Hill wolves that spook the wagon horses
The burned hunting lodge, the Greycoats' locus, friendly
breadcrumbs: South to Tennely House in the Southern heartland, from the letter that names the heir
d908slex.site: The valley floor beside the north stream, under the crags.
d908slex.situation: A hidden valley: the Tennelys' summer house, kept out of view of the farms, holding the way up to the north pass.
d908slex.scene: The grain road comes up from the farms and the west road from the river both end in the courtyard before the hall, where the Tennelys' sword statue still stands by the well and Council banners hang at the door. The hall, the Tennelys' old summer house, closes the courtyard on the north, its tables now the garrison's and its library Liesel Fairlie's. The granary and the big barn stand on the east side, sacks and supply crates at their doors, where Rafe Saddler counts the grain. The barracks stand west of the hall, with a weapon rack and archery targets by the summer garden, where a gazebo and old statues are left over from the Tennelys. Bram Oakes's inn faces the courtyard from the south-west, where the roads meet, and the stable lies south-east with a trough for the wagon horses. A guard tower watches the way north to the pass, and the graveyard lies east in the meadow, off the road.

fx4u6pd9.name: Northgate
fx4u6pd9.what: A palisaded trading post shared with Nordish herders.
fx4u6pd9.where: On the coast plain under the north-west crags, where Northgate beck comes down to the north stream, on the north road up the coast to the Northwest coast.
fx4u6pd9.mood: Friendly and competing. Nordish herds push south into Angean pasture.
people: Ottar Haldsson, Nordish trader, genial and slippery
lines: The north road (8-10): the pasture fight, wolves from the hills, and the tithe's skimmed grain in Ottar's wagon
nearby: The hill bear that took a calf
breadcrumbs: A sideways nod to the Northwest coast (18-28), not a quest to go now
fx4u6pd9.site: The beck's bank on the flat below the crags, a short walk from the sea.
fx4u6pd9.situation: A gap: the north road's only easy way between the crags and the sea.
fx4u6pd9.scene: A log palisade on the beck's bank below the crags, with gates on the north road, the south road from the farms and the river road from the east, and towers at its north-east and south-west corners. Inside, the roads meet by a rune stone the Nordish raised at the north gate. Hild Gunnar's-daughter's alehouse stands on the west side, where Arnbjorn the skald sings for his drink, and Ottar Haldsson's trading hall south of it, with barrels, sacks and his handcart in the yard. The Nordish herders camp in the north-east corner in big tents round a fire, with Sigrun Asa's-daughter, and their calves are penned in the south-east corner by a trough and a haystack. A well stands between. The graveyard lies outside the west wall, toward the sea, off the road.

ytkenc47.name: Wrackholm
ytkenc47.what: A fishing village of two or three cottages and a drying rack on the cove under Gull Head.
ytkenc47.where: On the beach of the cove on the west coast, north of Gull Head, up the coast from Brightford.
ytkenc47.mood: Scared and stubborn. The dead come up the beach at night, and nobody will leave the boats.
people: Marra Tidwell, the net-mender who speaks for the village
lines: The drowned dead (6-8): the dead from the old wreck, and the necromancer in the sea-cave
nearby: The Old Wreck off Gull Head, where the dead come from
The sea-cave at the foot of Gull Head's cliff, reached from the beach south of it
ytkenc47.site: Low beach ground on the cove, out of sight of the other hubs behind Gull Head and the hill north of it.
ytkenc47.situation: Off the coast road by a short lane, between Brightford and Northgate.
ytkenc47.scene: The lane from the coast road ends above the beach, at three thatched cottages round a well on the low ground of the cove. Marra Tidwell's cottage, where travellers sleep behind a barred door, faces the beach; Tam Fenn's stands north of it, with a woodshed behind, and Petra Skerry tans hides outside the third, to the south-east. Fish drying racks, net racks and crates line the beach, with beached and upturned boats and crab pots, and a short dock runs out into the cove. The village dead lie in a small fenced plot of grave mounds and cairns up the rise to the north-east, off the lane.

nhcorra1.name: Abbess Corra Lindqvist
nhcorra1.voice: Short, kind sentences, often a joke against herself. Calls every Waker "love".
nhcorra1.notes: Greets the new-woken. Short of hands since the levy took the lay brothers, and won't complain of it in front of the assessor. Tells the story of Brother Ansel, and sends Wakers on to Hallam's cross.

nhbranni.name: Keeper Brannick
nhbranni.voice: Clipped orders, soldier's words. Calls you "sleeper" until you've fought something.
nhbranni.notes: The Abbey's warden, the only keeper who can fight, and now the only one who can lift a sack. Foxes and the kobold sneaks.

nhnell01.name: Keeper Nell Sallow
nhnell01.voice: Quick, talks while working, names every plant she hands you.
nhnell01.notes: The herbalist. Makes rushlights since the candles went missing, and the sleeping draught for the first dream.

nhaubin1.name: Keeper Aubin
nhaubin1.voice: Soft and slow, leaves sentences unfinished, answers a question with a question.
nhaubin1.notes: The dream-keeper. Studies the wisps and the falls, and sets Wakers to sleep by the water. Says not every Waker comes to in the dormitory, and won't say more; he's heard the word "dreamers" and won't use it.

nhpell01.name: Assessor Pell Duvane
nhpell01.voice: Precise, apologetic, quotes the Council's rules by number.
nhpell01.notes: The Council's assessor, counting the Abbey's stores for the tithe. Honest: his count is true, which Hallam's will find isn't so everywhere.

nhwenna1.name: Keeper Hilde Ashby
nhwenna1.voice: Runs on, apologises for running on, runs on again.
nhwenna1.notes: The hosteller. Keeps the refectory and the cells, feeds and beds the new-woken, and sells what the Abbey can spare. Counts the bread twice since the assessor came.

nhtobin1.name: Grandsire Tobin Hallam
nhtobin1.voice: Long stories that wander off, "in the old lord's day", and a wink when he's hiding something.
nhtobin1.notes: Wenna's grandfather, who remembers the Tennelys fondly and the Council not at all. Brews hedge-apple cider, the one thing the Council doesn't count. Says the old lord's luck "came out of the ground". Knows Tennely grey when he sees it, and won't say who's wearing it.

nhodile1.name: Reeve Odile Marchbank
nhodile1.voice: Measured, formal, chooses every word; softens only in private.
nhodile1.notes: The Council's reeve at Brightford. Believes in the revolution's promises and is ashamed of how they've gone. Holds the true standard measure, and sets you to check Varn Ostrey's.

nhvarn01.name: Varn Ostrey
nhvarn01.voice: Fast and fussy, all figures; apologises before he's accused.
nhvarn01.notes: The tithe collector. His scales read a tenth light, by order he was given and never questioned. Moved to keep the Abbey's books with Assessor Duvane, not punished.

nhpike01.name: Sergeant Ada Pike
nhpike01.voice: Barked sentences, militia slang, no patience for "why".
nhpike01.notes: Runs Brightford's militia post and lock-up with half her men gone to the gap. Takes the grey-coated robbers for Greycoats.

nhmoll01.name: Moll Abernathy
nhmoll01.voice: Loud and fond, gossip in every answer, calls everyone by a pet name.
nhmoll01.notes: The innkeeper. Hears everything, from the loggers' grumbling to the militia's news.

nhberti1.name: Old Bertil
nhberti1.voice: Slow, formal, old soldier's words; stands when he talks of the old lord.
nhberti1.notes: An old guard veteran who stayed in town. Visits Jory Venn in the lock-up. Says the old lord never let anyone into the cellars.

nhjory01.name: Jory Venn
nhjory01.voice: Cheerful insolence through the bars; turns serious about the coat.
nhjory01.notes: A Greycoat in Brightford's lock-up, taken for a robbery he didn't do. Knows a false grey coat from a real one.

nhhetti1.name: Hettie Croft
nhhetti1.voice: Prim, quotes the plaque from memory.
nhhetti1.notes: Wants the toppled statue's plaque kept, whatever she thinks of the Tennelys: it's the town's history.

nhcrake1.name: Ludo Crake
nhcrake1.voice: Haggling patter, prices everything he sees.
nhcrake1.notes: The scrap dealer. Wants the statue's plaque sold, and has the Hallams' shrine bell, which the militia sold him for the gap.

nhtarra1.name: Foreman Gus Tarrant
nhtarra1.voice: Shouts over saws, swears at the Council, laughs easily.
nhtarra1.notes: Runs Cliffside camp's loggers. Sick of the Council's quotas and of arrows from the cliff top.

nhhale01.name: Captain Wystan Hale
nhhale01.voice: Clipped and formal, never says what he thinks.
nhhale01.notes: The granary's captain. Served the Tennelys and serves the Council now, and guards their old summer house for it.

nhithri1.name: Ithriel
nhithri1.voice: Few words, old-fashioned and exact; never uses a name until she's sure of you.
nhithri1.notes: An elven warden of the High forest, who comes down to the chute's ledge once, to be heard. Shows that the cutting undermines the trees that hold the cliff. Warns that the Abbey sits "on the doorstep of a wound", and won't explain.

nhrook01.name: Captain Elsbet Rook
nhrook01.voice: Quiet, plain words, an old officer's courtesy; asks before she tells.
nhrook01.notes: The Greycoats' captain, at the burned hunting lodge in the hills above Tennely Hall. Thanks you for Slade with a letter that names the Tennely heir. Served beside Captain Hale once.

nhottar1.name: Ottar Haldsson
nhottar1.voice: Warm, loud and full of jokes; never quite answers what he's asked.
nhottar1.notes: Nordish trader at Northgate. Buys grain cheap off the north road and sells it north, and doesn't ask where it came from.

nhsigru1.name: Sigrun Asa's-daughter
nhsigru1.voice: Short and plain; says what her herd needs and expects the same back.
nhsigru1.notes: Nordish herder at Northgate. Her herd grazes the meadow south of the gap, which the Angean farmers call theirs. Losing calves to the hill wolves and the bear.

nharnbj1.name: Arnbjorn the skald
nharnbj1.voice: Speaks in turns of phrase, half of them borrowed from old songs.
nharnbj1.notes: Nordish skald at Northgate. Knows the old songs of the meadow and the coast to the north-west, and puts new deeds into verse.

wrmarra1.name: Marra Tidwell
wrmarra1.voice: Plain and short, mending as she talks.
wrmarra1.notes: Speaks for the village. Her grandson Corwin went to Brightford to learn his letters and came back strange. She knows it's him in the sea-cave before she says so.

wrjory01.name: Tam Fenn
wrjory01.voice: Talks fast and low, keeps glancing at the water.
wrjory01.notes: A fisherman who saw the dead walk up out of the water by the wreck. Still takes his boat out by day, and teaches Wakers to fish.

wrcorwn1.name: Corwin Tidwell
wrcorwn1.voice: Bookish, sure he's cleverer than the village.
wrcorwn1.notes: A weak necromancer, Marra's grandson. Raises the drowned dead from the old wreck, from the chamber in the sea-cave. A hostile NPC, the chain's end.

hxwenna1.name: Wenna Hallam
hxwenna1.voice: Measured and level, every word weighed like grain. Never raises her voice; never needs to.
hxwenna1.notes: Head of the Hallams, and so of the crossroads. Knows the Council's measure is false and can't prove it yet. Starts the tithe.

hxama001.name: Ama Rusk
hxama001.voice: Asks two questions for every one she answers.
hxama001.notes: The Rusks take in travellers since the tithe took the harvest. Feeds Wakers, beds them, and hears all the gossip of the crossroads.

hxdunst1.name: Dunstan Cobb
hxdunst1.voice: Few words, most of them about wood.
hxdunst1.notes: Wheelwright and smith of the Cobbs. Mends carts, ploughs and Wakers' gear, and sells what a traveller needs.

hxorla01.name: Orla Cobb
hxorla01.voice: Short and wry, always looking past you at the tree line.
hxorla01.notes: Dunstan's sister, who hunts the hills for the pot. Teaches Wakers to skin what they kill.

bfgarow1.name: Garrow Fenwick
bfgarow1.voice: Talks while he hammers, a word a blow.
bfgarow1.notes: Brightford's smith. Shoes the militia's horses, mends Wakers' arms and armor, and teaches the forge to anyone who'll sweat at it.

bftilda1.name: Tilda Brack
bftilda1.voice: Quick tallies under her breath; never gives credit.
bftilda1.notes: Keeps Brightford's stone shop: packs, rope, thread and vials, all a traveller needs. Rather the Council than the Tennelys, as long as it pays.

bfedric1.name: Edric Lowe
bfedric1.voice: Soft and precise, pins in his mouth.
bfedric1.notes: The tailor. Sews for the town and the militia, sells cloth and thread, and teaches the needle.

bfwilma1.name: Wilma Rooke
bfwilma1.voice: Dry and knowing, sniffs at everything before she answers.
bfwilma1.notes: The apothecary. Brews for the town's coughs and the militia's wounds, buys herbs off the Abbey, and teaches the still.

bfjessa1.name: Jessa Thorne
bfjessa1.voice: Calls her prices across the square like a challenge.
bfjessa1.notes: Keeps a market stall of leather jerkins, boots and bows, most of it her brother's work from the hills.

hxbryn01.name: Bryn Cobb
hxbryn01.voice: Slow and easy, laughs at his own jokes before the end.
hxbryn01.notes: The youngest Cobb. Digs the stone and iron out of the bank by the stream for Dunstan's forge, and shows Wakers how to swing a pick.

hxmaud01.name: Gran Maud Rusk
hxmaud01.voice: Scolds and doctors in the same breath.
hxmaud01.notes: Ama's mother. Gathers herbs along the hedges and field edges for the farm's ills, and teaches Wakers what to pick and what to leave.

wrpetra1.name: Petra Skerry
wrpetra1.voice: Spits for luck before she answers.
wrpetra1.notes: Tans sealskin and fish leather on the racks behind her cottage, sells hides and thread, and teaches Wakers the work.

clnan001.name: Nan Brewis
clnan001.voice: Bellows across the camp, softens over a bowl.
clnan001.notes: The camp's cook. Feeds the loggers from the cookhouse, keeps the fire going all night, and finds a blanket by it for any Waker who needs one.

cldell01.name: Dell Marrow
cldell01.voice: Counts out loud, then counts again.
cldell01.notes: The camp's quartermaster. Hands out rope, sacks and whetstones against the Council's tally, mends the loggers' gear, and will sell to Wakers if they pay in coin.

clossie1.name: Ossie Wrenfield
clossie1.voice: Thinks aloud in gears and pulleys, loses the thread, finds it again.
clossie1.notes: The sawwright. Built the camp's crane and the chute, keeps the mill's saws running, and teaches Wakers to make machines.

thbram01.name: Bram Oakes
thbram01.voice: Easy and warm, and listens to the wagoners more than he talks.
thbram01.notes: Keeps the wagoners' inn by the grain road's end. Was the Tennelys' groom once, and still knows which horses spook at wolves. Rents a bed to any Waker with coin, and some without.

thrafe01.name: Rafe Saddler
thrafe01.voice: Short sentences, each one a list.
thrafe01.notes: The garrison's quartermaster. Counts the grain in and the wagons out, mends the guards' kit, and sells spare gear and supplies to Wakers for coin the Council never sees.

thlies01.name: Liesel Fairlie
thlies01.voice: Soft and exact, as if dictating to a clerk.
thlies01.notes: Kept the Tennelys' books and their warded stores, and stayed on when the Council took the house. Still keeps the old wards on the hall, and teaches Wakers to bind power into cloth and steel.

nghild01.name: Hild Gunnar's-daughter
nghild01.voice: Laughs from the belly, and tells you what you owe in the same breath.
nghild01.notes: Keeps Northgate's alehouse, where Nordish herders and Angean drovers drink at the same tables. Brews her own mead, and gives any Waker a bench by the fire for the night.

nhcometo.name: Come to
nhcometo.summary: You come to in the dormitory, and the Abbess puts you to work.
nhcometo.objectives: Talk to Keeper Brannick in the yard.
nhcometo.why: The levy took the lay brothers for the gap, and the Abbey needs hands. Brannick wants to see whether you can hold a stick.

nhfoxes1.name: Foxes at the hens
nhfoxes1.summary: Foxes come up from the lakeshore for the Abbey's hens.
nhfoxes1.why: Brannick has nobody to sit up with the hens now the lay brothers are gone, and the Abbey can't spare a bird.

nhrushes.name: Rushlights
nhrushes.summary: The chapel's candles keep going missing, so Nell makes rushlights.
nhrushes.objectives: Gather 8 lamp rushes along the lakeshore.
nhrushes.why: Rushes dipped in fat burn nearly as well as candles, and nobody steals them. Nell can't leave the herb garden to cut them herself.

nhwisps1.name: Thin wisps
nhwisps1.summary: Dream-wisps drift from the falls pool, more each year.
nhwisps1.objectives: Bring 6 wisp-glimmers from dream-wisps at the falls pool.
nhwisps1.why: Aubin wants to know what the wisps are made of, and why there are more of them. He won't say what he fears.

nhdroot1.name: Dreamroot
nhdroot1.summary: Nell's sleeping draught needs dreamroot, which grows only in the falls pool's shallows.
nhdroot1.objectives: Gather 5 dreamroot in the falls pool's shallows.
nhdroot1.why: Aubin has asked for a draught for you. Dreamroot only grows where the Dream's water runs, and the wisps make Nell's skin crawl.

nhansel1.name: Who walked into the water
nhansel1.summary: Before he lets you sleep by the water, Aubin wants you to hear about Brother Ansel.
nhansel1.objectives: Ask Abbess Corra about Brother Ansel, at his stone in the chapel garden.
nhansel1.why: Aubin won't tell it himself. Ansel was a dream-keeper who walked into the water in his sleep thirty years ago, and the Abbess wants every Waker to know the falls take people.

nhdream1.name: The first dream
nhdream1.summary: Aubin sets you to sleep by the falls pool for your first dream.
nhdream1.objectives: Drink Nell's draught and sleep on the stone at the falls pool's edge. Tell Aubin what you dreamed.
nhdream1.why: Every Waker has a first dream, and Aubin keeps a book of them. Yours is of water and falling, as they all are lately, and he writes it down without a word.

nhsendof.name: The Abbey's neighbours
nhsendof.summary: The Abbess sends you out along the north shore to Hallam's cross.
nhsendof.objectives: Take a bundle of Nell's rushlights to Wenna Hallam at Hallam's cross.
nhsendof.why: The Hallams are the Abbey's neighbours and are behind on their tithe, and the Abbess owes them for seed barley. She thinks you've done all the Abbey can teach you.

nhcandle.name: Missing candles
nhcandle.summary: Kobold sneaks from burrows under the cliff steal the chapel's candles.
nhcandle.objectives: Kill kobold sneaks at their burrows in the cliff's north end, and bring back 6 stolen candles.
nhcandle.why: The candles are the chapel's, bought dear, and the assessor has them on his list. Brannick would rather have them back than explain.

nhtallow.name: Tallowtooth
nhtallow.summary: The sneaks answer to a fat kobold who sits on the candles in the deepest burrow.
nhtallow.objectives: Kill Tallowtooth in the deepest of the sneaks' burrows and bring back his glass lantern.
nhtallow.why: Brannick says the sneaks won't stop while their chief has a hoard to grow. Take the lantern, so they've nothing to steal for.

nhglass1.name: Not kobold glass
nhglass1.summary: The sneaks drop shards of glass that glow on their own.
nhglass1.objectives: Take a glowing shard from the sneaks to Keeper Aubin.
nhglass1.why: Brannick has never seen kobolds make anything that fine. Aubin knows old glass when he sees it: elves' work from the Age of Light, carried out from somewhere deep in the cliff.

nhcount1.name: The assessor's count
nhcount1.summary: The Council's assessor is counting the Abbey's stores, and needs someone to climb.
nhcount1.objectives: Count the barrels in the cellar, the sacks in the granary loft and the hams in the smokehouse.
nhcount1.why: Pell must count the Abbey's stores for the tithe and has a bad knee for ladders. He wants the count true either way: the Council's rule is a tenth of what's there, not a tenth of a guess.

nhsalve1.name: Nell's salve
nhsalve1.summary: Nell has a salve for the assessor's knee.
nhsalve1.objectives: Take Nell's salve to Assessor Pell Duvane.
nhsalve1.why: Nell doesn't like the Council, but she won't let a man limp. She'd rather not be thanked for it.

nhpalefi.name: Pale fish
nhpalefi.summary: Pale, eyeless fish swim in the shallows by the falls, where no fish like them used to be.
nhpalefi.objectives: Bring 4 pale fish from the eyeless fry in the falls pool's shallows.
nhpalefi.why: Aubin wants them for his book, beside the first dreams. He doesn't say what made them, or how big the thing is that breeds them.

hcrats01.name: Rats in the barns
hcrats01.summary: Rats in the Hallams' barns eat into the grain they owe.
hcrats01.objectives: Kill 8 barn rats in the Hallams' barns.
hcrats01.why: Every sack the rats get into is a sack short at the count, and the Hallams are short already. Wenna has no cat that'll face them.

hcboars1.name: Boars in the barley
hcboars1.summary: Boars come down off the rise at night and root up the barley.
hcboars1.objectives: Bring 5 boar hides from the boars in the barley.
hcboars1.why: The boars cost the Hallams a row a night, and the cart cover's in rags. Wenna would have both problems gone at once.

hcbristl.name: Old Bristle
hcbristl.summary: A big old boar leads the others down, and breaks the hedges to do it.
hcbristl.objectives: Kill Old Bristle at the edge of the rise and bring back his tusks.
hcbristl.why: The young boars follow him. With him gone they'll keep to the woods, and Tobin wants the tusks over the door.

hcapples.name: Hedge apples
hcapples.summary: Tobin brews cider from the hedge apples, the one thing the Council doesn't count.
hcapples.objectives: Gather 10 hedge apples along the farms' hedges.
hcapples.why: The cider is the Hallams' one thing to sell that the tithe doesn't touch, and Tobin's back won't let him reach the high branches.

hcsacks1.name: Short sacks
hcsacks1.summary: The Council's collector counted the Hallams' sacks short. Wenna says they're full.
hcsacks1.objectives: Weigh 3 of the Hallams' tithe sacks on the farm's steelyard.
hcsacks1.why: Varn Ostrey's scales said the Hallams owe another cart. Wenna wants someone who isn't a Hallam to see the sacks are full, so the reeve can't call it farmers' lying.

hcreeve1.name: To the reeve
hcreeve1.summary: With the sacks weighed, Wenna sends her complaint to Brightford.
hcreeve1.objectives: Take the Hallams' complaint and a sealed tithe sack to Reeve Odile Marchbank in Brightford.
hcreeve1.why: The reeve holds the Council's true measure. Wenna doesn't trust her, but she trusts Varn less, and you saw the sacks weighed.

hcgrain1.name: Grain on the step
hcgrain1.summary: Some mornings there's a sack of grain on the Hallams' step, and nobody saw who left it.
hcgrain1.objectives: Search the hedge gap behind the shrine, where whoever leaves the grain comes and goes, and bring Tobin what you find.
hcgrain1.why: Tobin wants to know who's feeding them before the Council asks. You find a torn scrap of grey wool. Tobin knows Tennely grey, says it's "a kindness from the old days", and won't say more.

bfstand1.name: The true measure
bfstand1.summary: Farmers up the road say Varn's scales weigh their sacks light, and the reeve means to test it.
bfstand1.objectives: Weigh the reeve's standard weight on Varn's scales in the tithe barn.
bfstand1.why: Odile holds the Council's true weight and won't accuse anyone on a farmer's word. The scales read a tenth light.

bfsouth1.name: Farms south of the road
bfsouth1.summary: If Varn's scales are light for the Hallams, they're light for everyone.
bfsouth1.objectives: Ask the 3 farms south of the road what Varn's scales made of their sacks.
bfsouth1.why: Odile needs more than one farm before she brings it to the Council. Each farm was counted short by the same tenth.
areas: the farms south of the road

bfledger.name: Varn's ledger
bfledger.summary: A tenth extra from every farm has to go somewhere.
bfledger.objectives: Take Varn's ledger from the tithe barn while he's at the inn.
bfledger.why: Odile wants to see where the extra went before Varn can explain it away. The ledger shows it loaded onto the grain wagons to Tennely Hall, by an order Varn never questioned.

bfvarn01.name: Moved, not punished
bfvarn01.summary: Varn only followed his orders, and Odile won't hang a clerk for them.
bfvarn01.objectives: Take the reeve's order to Varn Ostrey: he's to keep the Abbey's books with Assessor Duvane.
bfvarn01.why: Odile thinks the scales were set by someone above Varn, and a frightened clerk out of the way is safer than one in a cell. Where the extra grain went is still open.

bfrobber.name: Grey coats on the north road
bfrobber.summary: Robbers in grey coats are stopping carts on the north road.
bfrobber.objectives: Kill the grey-coated robbers on the north road and bring back 5 of the notched sticks they carry.
bfrobber.why: Pike calls them Greycoats and wants them gone before the grain wagons stop. Every robber carries a stick notched with a tally, and she can't read them.

bfjory01.name: The man in the lock-up
bfjory01.summary: Old Bertil says the north road's robbers aren't Greycoats, and Jory Venn can prove it.
bfjory01.objectives: Take a robber's grey coat to Jory Venn in the lock-up.
bfjory01.why: Bertil visits Jory, who was taken for a robbery he didn't do. Jory turns the coat in his hands: the dye's wrong, the cut's wrong, it's made to look like Tennely grey.

bfjory02.name: Jory's message
bfjory02.summary: Jory has a message for the granary's captain, who wore the grey once.
bfjory02.objectives: Take Jory's message to Captain Wystan Hale at Tennely Hall.
bfjory02.why: Jory says somebody wants the Greycoats blamed, and the grain wagons to Tennely Hall are what the robbers are after. Hale served the Tennelys, and Jory thinks he'll listen.

bfeels01.name: Eels at the ford
bfeels01.summary: Moll's eel pie is the inn's best, and she's out of eels.
bfeels01.objectives: Bring 6 eels from the ford's eels.
bfeels01.why: Her eel man went with the levy. Moll will feed you for a week on it.

bfwolves.name: South bank wolves
bfwolves.summary: Wolves in the south bank woods go for travellers at the ford.
bfwolves.objectives: Bring 6 wolf pelts from the south bank woods.
bfwolves.why: Pike has no men to spare for the ford, so she pays a bounty by the pelt instead.

bfplaque.name: The old lord's plaque
bfplaque.summary: The Tennelys' statue lies toppled in the square, and its plaque is about to be sold for scrap.
bfplaque.objectives: Prise the plaque off the toppled statue's plinth before Ludo Crake does.
bfplaque.why: Hettie doesn't love the Tennelys, but the plaque is the town's history, and the town was Tennelford for a hundred years.

bfbell01.name: Iron for a bell
bfbell01.summary: Ludo has the Hallams' shrine bell, bought from the militia for the gap. He'll trade it for its weight in iron.
bfbell01.objectives: Gather 6 lots of old iron from the wrecked carts along the north road.
bfbell01.why: Ludo sells by weight and can't sell a bell anyone would recognise. He'd sooner have iron, and you'd sooner the Hallams had their bell.

bfbell02.name: The shrine's bell
bfbell02.summary: With the iron traded, the Hallams' bell can go home.
bfbell02.objectives: Take the shrine bell back to Grandsire Tobin at Hallam's cross, on your way east or north.
bfbell02.why: Ludo's glad to see it gone. Tobin rang that bell for the old lord's wedding.

bfcamp01.name: Hands for the camp
bfcamp01.summary: The loggers drinking at Moll's say Cliffside camp needs hands.
bfcamp01.objectives: Go east past Hallam's cross to Cliffside camp and talk to Foreman Gus Tarrant.
bfcamp01.why: The Council's quota is due and the arrows from the cliff top have the loggers scared off the ledge. Moll likes the loggers, and their custom.

bfguard1.name: A guard for the granary
bfguard1.summary: Tennely Hall's granary is short of guards with the robbers about.
bfguard1.objectives: Go north up the grain road to Tennely Hall and report to Captain Wystan Hale.
bfguard1.why: Pike can't spare any of her own, so she sends anyone who can fight.

csdig01.name: Kobolds at the diggings
csdig01.summary: Kobolds dig into the cliff foot beside the camp and come out at night for the loggers' lamps and tools.
csdig01.objectives: Kill 8 kobold diggers outside the diggings.
csdig01.why: Tarrant loses a lamp or an axe a night, and the quota won't wait for new ones.

csglass1.name: Glass in the dark
csglass1.summary: The kobolds inside carry shards of glass that glow on their own, like the ones at the Abbey.
csglass1.objectives: Bring 8 glowing shards from the kobolds inside the diggings.
csglass1.why: Tarrant thinks the glass is what they're digging for, and wants to know how much is in there before the Council does.

csshrin1.name: The glass shrines
csshrin1.summary: Deeper in, the kobolds have built shrines round heaps of the glass and bow to them.
csshrin1.objectives: Topple 3 glass shrines in the diggings.
csshrin1.why: The kobolds fight hardest round the shrines. Tarrant reckons that without them they'll lose heart and keep to their holes.

csglowm1.name: The Glowmother
csglowm1.summary: The kobolds' Glowmother hoards the glass in a chamber they broke into at the back of the diggings, cut and lined by someone long before them.
csglowm1.objectives: Kill the Glowmother in the glass chamber and bring back her glass crown.
csglowm1.why: With the shrines down, she's what keeps them digging. Her kobolds speak of "the Wickfather below", and Tarrant doesn't like the sound of it.

csrock01.name: Cold air
csrock01.summary: The deepest tunnel runs on past the glass chamber, and the kobolds were still digging it.
csrock01.objectives: Go to the end of the deepest tunnel and see what the kobolds were digging toward.
csrock01.why: Tarrant won't send a logger down there. It ends at a rockfall with cold, wet air coming through and a faint singing behind it, and he means to wall it up.

csarrow1.name: Arrows at the chute
csarrow1.summary: Arrows from the cliff top have stopped the log chute.
csarrow1.objectives: Climb to the chute's head on the ledge and find what the arrows are aimed at.
csarrow1.why: Tarrant's men won't go up while the arrows fly, and the quota's due. The arrows all land in the same stumps, the newest cut, and never in a man.

csanswe1.name: An answer
csanswe1.summary: Tarrant wants the arrows answered, and you'd rather talk than shoot.
csanswe1.objectives: Take Tarrant's message to the chute's head and wait for whoever comes down.
csanswe1.why: Tarrant would sooner know what they want than lose a man finding out. The elven warden Ithriel comes down to the ledge, once.

csroots1.name: What holds the cliff
csroots1.summary: Ithriel says the camp is cutting the trees that hold the cliff together.
csroots1.objectives: Look at 3 places along the ledge where the ground has slumped since the cutting began.
csroots1.why: She won't argue with loggers, only show them. The roots go down into the cliff, and where the trees came out, the rock is coming away.

csline01.name: A no-cut line
csline01.summary: Ithriel marks a line the loggers mustn't cut past.
csline01.objectives: Tell Foreman Tarrant where Ithriel's line runs, and what you saw on the ledge.
csline01.why: The arrows stop if the line holds. Tarrant swears at the Council's quota and agrees, since a falling cliff costs more than a short year.

csspide1.name: Rope for the chute
csspide1.summary: The chute's ropes rot in the damp, and the cliff-foot spiders spin the best line there is.
csspide1.objectives: Bring 6 coils of silk from the cliff-foot spiders.
csspide1.why: Spider silk holds a log better than hemp and doesn't rot. Nobody at the camp will go near the spiders.

thtally1.name: Slade's tally
thtally1.summary: Robbers in grey coats are taking the grain wagons. Hale has lost two this month.
thtally1.objectives: Kill Slade's tallyman in the hills above the grain road and bring back his tally board.
thtally1.why: Hale won't say what he thinks of the grey coats, but he wants proof of who wears them. The board counts every wagon taken, and marks the way back to a camp in the hills east.

thcamp01.name: Slade's band
thcamp01.summary: Slade's band camps in the hills east of the valley, on a shelf above the steep foot.
thcamp01.objectives: Kill 10 of Slade's band at his camp.
thcamp01.why: Hale can't take the garrison off the granary. Thin the band, and Slade will have to come out himself.

thslade1.name: Slade
thslade1.summary: Slade keeps the camp's tally in a book, and keeps the book on him.
thslade1.objectives: Kill Slade at his camp and bring back his tally book.
thslade1.why: With Slade gone the band breaks up. The book shows grain taken in grey coats and sold on, and it clears every Greycoat the Council has blamed.

thlodge1.name: The burned lodge
thlodge1.summary: Hale quietly asks you to take Slade's book somewhere he can't be seen going.
thlodge1.objectives: Take Slade's tally book to Captain Elsbet Rook at the burned hunting lodge.
thlodge1.why: The book clears the Greycoats, and Hale served with Rook before the revolution. Rook thanks you with a letter that names the Tennely heir, and asks you to keep it.

thcount1.name: The granary's count
thcount1.summary: Varn's ledger says a tenth extra went to Tennely Hall. Hale says it never came.
thcount1.objectives: Count the sacks in the granary's 3 bays against the wagon book.
thcount1.why: Hale keeps his count to the sack, and won't be called a thief. The granary holds what the Council asked, and not a sack more: the extra left Brightford and never got here.

thruts01.name: Ruts over the saddle
thruts01.summary: Some wagons come in lighter than they left Brightford, and late.
thruts01.objectives: Follow the wagon ruts that turn off the grain road over the saddle, to where they meet the north road.
thruts01.why: Hale wants to know where his missing sacks go before he writes to the Council. The ruts run west toward Northgate, where the Nordish traders buy grain.

thwolve1.name: Spooked horses
thwolve1.summary: Hill wolves come down to the grain road and spook the wagon horses.
thwolve1.objectives: Kill 8 hill wolves along the valley's edge.
thwolve1.why: A bolting team can lose a wagon in the brook. Hale has lost one that way already, and blames the wolves louder than the robbers.

ngstone1.name: The boundary stones
ngstone1.summary: The Angean farmers say the meadow south of the gap is theirs, and Sigrun's herd has no right to it.
ngstone1.objectives: Read the 3 old boundary stones in the north meadow.
ngstone1.why: The stones are older than the farms. Their marks name the meadow common grazing, for any herd that keeps the road open.

ngcalf01.name: Taken calves
ngcalf01.summary: Hill wolves take calves from both herds, Nordish and Angean, and drag them up into the hills.
ngcalf01.objectives: Kill north road wolves and bring back 5 calf bells.
ngcalf01.why: Every bell is a calf lost. Sigrun means to give the Angean ones back to their farmers, to show the wolves don't care whose herd it is.

ngbear01.name: The hill bear
ngbear01.summary: A hill bear took a calf from under the palisade, and the wolves follow where it goes.
ngbear01.objectives: Kill the hill bear in its den in the western hills and bring back its hide.
ngbear01.why: With the bear gone the wolves scatter. Both herds owe the same hunter, and that's a thing to build on.

ngsaga01.name: A verse for the meadow
ngsaga01.summary: Sigrun wants the meadow shared, and wants it said where both sides will hear.
ngsaga01.objectives: Tell Arnbjorn the skald about the stones, the calves and the bear.
ngsaga01.why: A song is how the Nordish keep a promise. Arnbjorn makes the verse, and sings of the coast to the north-west while he's at it, where the old songs came from.

ngwagon1.name: Ottar's wagon
ngwagon1.summary: Ottar sells more grain north than any farm round here grows for sale.
ngwagon1.objectives: Look under the hides in Ottar's wagon.
ngwagon1.why: Sigrun has wondered for a season. Under the hides are sacks stamped with Brightford's tithe mark.

ngottar1.name: A slippery trader
ngottar1.summary: Ottar laughs off most questions, but tithe sacks are hard to laugh off.
ngottar1.objectives: Ask Ottar Haldsson where the tithe sacks came from.
ngottar1.why: He bought them honestly, he says, from a Council carter who comes over the saddle at night. He has the bill of sale, and he'd rather you had it than the Council found it on him.

ngbill01.name: The bill of sale
ngbill01.summary: Ottar's bill of sale names the carter and the price.
ngbill01.objectives: Take Ottar's bill of sale to Captain Hale at Tennely Hall.
ngbill01.why: Hale's missing sacks have a seller now, and it isn't the Greycoats. He writes to the Council with the bill, and with Varn's ledger beside it.

hcwebs01.name: Webs in the ruin
hcwebs01.summary: Spiders have spun webs through Crumbling Ruin, at the rise's south-west foot, where the Hallams graze sheep in summer.
hcwebs01.objectives: Burn 5 web nests in and round Crumbling Ruin.
hcwebs01.why: Tobin lost two ewes there last year, wrapped and hung. He'd go himself if his knees let him.

bfshell1.name: Shells for the kiln
bfshell1.summary: Hettie burns shells for lime to whitewash the plaques.
bfshell1.objectives: Bring 8 crab shells from the crabs on the coast meadows.
bfshell1.why: The levy took the lad who gathered them. Crabs have come up the meadows since.

bftoads1.name: Toads in the cress
bftoads1.summary: Toads have taken over the cress beds Bertil cuts along the river.
bftoads1.objectives: Kill 8 toads in the river meadows' cress beds.
bftoads1.why: He sells the cress at the ford. Without it he has nothing to sell.

cschalk1.name: Chalk marks
cschalk1.summary: Kobold scouts mark the loggers' trees with chalk, counting them.
cschalk1.objectives: Bring 5 chalk tallies from the kobold scouts in the loggers' valley.
cschalk1.why: Tarrant wants to know what they're counting, and why so many.

ngfat001.name: Fat for the lamps
ngfat001.summary: Northgate's lamps burn bear fat, and the hall is almost out.
ngfat001.objectives: Bring 6 rounds of bear fat from the bears in the western hills.
ngfat001.why: The hunters who'd fetch it are watching the north road for the wolves.

ngdrift1.name: Driftwood
ngdrift1.summary: Ottar needs dry wood to smoke his catch, and the north coast is thick with it.
ngdrift1.objectives: Gather 8 bundles of driftwood along the north coast.
ngdrift1.why: Crabs the size of shields work the tideline. Ottar won't go past them.

wrbeach1.name: Dead on the beach
wrbeach1.summary: The dead came up the beach again last night.
wrbeach1.objectives: Kill 6 drowned dead on the cove's beach.
wrbeach1.why: Marra wants the beach clear so the boats can go out.

wrwreck1.name: Where they come from
wrwreck1.summary: Jory saw them walk out of the sea by the old wreck.
wrwreck1.objectives: Go to the shore by the Old Wreck and see what comes out of it.
wrwreck1.why: Marra wants to know where they come from. You find the dead walking up out of the water, and fresh footprints going up the beach to Gull Head.

wrcave01.name: The sea-cave
wrcave01.summary: The footprints go into the sea-cave at the foot of Gull Head.
wrcave01.objectives: Go into the sea-cave and find who's raising the dead.
wrcave01.why: You find Corwin, Marra's grandson, with a book of the dead. He won't stop.

wrcorwn1.name: Marra's grandson
wrcorwn1.objectives: Defeat Corwin Tidwell in the sea-cave and bring Marra his book.
wrcorwn1.why: Marra wants it stopped, and the book burned.

newwoken.name: The new-woken (1-4)
newwoken.summary: At Wakewell Abbey the keepers get a new-woken Waker onto their feet with the chores the levy left undone, the hens' foxes, the herb garden and the dream-wisps drifting from the falls pool, until Keeper Aubin sets them to sleep by the water for their first dream, of water and falling, and sends them on to Hallam's cross; against the Dream's leak, its cause found as the falls.

glowdiggers.name: The glowdiggers (4-8)
glowdiggers.summary: Kobold sneaks steal the Abbey's candles and drop shards of glowing glass, which lead to Cliffside camp and the diggings in the cliff foot, where the kobolds have broken into an Age of Light chamber and worship its glass, until the Glowmother who hoards it is dealt with and the deepest tunnel ends at a rockfall with cold, wet air and singing behind it, the Underfall's upper reaches; against the kobolds, their locus dealt with.

tithe.name: The tithe (4-9)
tithe.summary: Hallam's farms come up short against the Council's measure, and Brightford's reeve sets you to check it, through Varn Ostrey's scales, his ledger and the farms south of the road, until the measure's shown false and Varn is moved, not punished, and the skim found at Northgate is set right; against the Council's tithe, its cause found.

greycoats.name: The Greycoats (6-10)
greycoats.summary: Grain left on Hallam's step by someone in a grey coat, robbers in grey coats on the north road and Jory Venn's message from Brightford's lock-up show two sets of grey coats, and the trail runs north to Tennely Hall, Slade's tally and his hill camp, until Slade is dealt with and the Greycoats' captain thanks you at the burned lodge with a letter that names the heir; against Slade's band, its locus dealt with.

wardens.name: The cliff wardens (7-10)
wardens.summary: Arrows from the cliff top stop the log chute at Cliffside camp, and the loggers want them answered, until the elven warden Ithriel comes down to the ledge and shows that the quota's cutting undermines the trees that hold the cliff, and Foreman Tarrant agrees a no-cut line; against the Council's tithe, its quotas' cause found.

northroad.name: The north road (8-10)
northroad.summary: At Northgate the Nordish herds push south into Angean pasture and the hill wolves and the bear take calves from both, until the pasture's shared and the grain in Ottar's wagon turns out to be the tithe's skim, sold north; against the Council's tithe, the skim's cause found.

drowned.name: The drowned dead (6-8)
drowned.summary: At Wrackholm the dead walk up out of the sea from an old wreck. The trail leads to the sea-cave under Gull Head, where Marra's grandson Corwin, a weak necromancer, is raising them.

sneaks-burrows.name: The sneaks' burrows
sneaks-burrows.what: A small warren of low runs under the Prow's south face, by the Abbey. Kobold sneaks throughout, with stolen candles; Tallowtooth in the deepest burrow, the north-east chamber, with his glass lantern.

the-diggings.name: The diggings
the-diggings.what: A kobold mine into the cliff foot east of Cliffside, up the basin from the camp. A gallery splits: the north side gallery holds the glass shrines; the main way goes on to the glass chamber, where the Glowmother is, and past it the deepest tunnel, cold air at its end.

bears-den.name: The hill bear's den
bears-den.what: One chamber in the north-west crags above the north road, between Northgate and Tennely Hall's valley, where the hill bear sleeps.

forces.name: The Council's tithe
forces.notes: The Council's reeve and tithe collector at Brightford, counting everybody's grain against a false measure. Requisitions go out to every farm and the Abbey, quotas to the loggers, and grain wagons up to the granary at Tennely Hall. Not an enemy: the heroes take its work, set its measure right and move its collector on, never fight it.

forces.name: Slade's band
forces.notes: Robbers in grey coats, so the Greycoats take the blame. Slade runs them from a camp in the hills east of Tennely Hall, robbing the north road and the grain wagons and keeping a tally of what he takes. The zone's villains, and the only people the heroes fight.

forces.name: The kobolds
forces.notes: Kobolds dug into an Age of Light chamber in the cliff foot above Cliffside camp and worship its glowing glass, under the Glowmother, who hoards it. Their sneaks have burrows in the cliff under the Prow by the Abbey and steal its candles. The honest monsters, with the wildlife.

forces.name: The Dream
forces.notes: Where the cascade falls into the lake, the Dream touches the world: dream-wisps and dreamroot at the falls pool, and the Wakers who come to at the Abbey across the water. Odd, not hostile. The Underfall's cave on the falls ledge, just past the border, is its source.

forces.name: The drowned dead
forces.notes: An old rotten wreck lies off Gull Head, and the dead walk up out of it onto the shore. A weak necromancer raises them from a sea-cave in the headland's cliff, over the cove. He came from Wrackholm, the fishing village they pester.
